A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConFIG and M-ConFIG work. Their main texts, appendices, equations, figures and tables are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original PINN experiments on four PDE cases and CelebA multi-task experiments, including numerical results, runtime comparisons and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original results for three challenging PDE problems and learning-rate and sampling ablations.

M1.justification: The normalized-gradient pseudoinverse, equal projection weighting, adaptive magnitude and alternating momentum updates remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1, 3 and 4. The additional experiments do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix A.11 adds five-dimensional Poisson, anisotropic multiscale heat transfer and chaotic KS problems. These substantially broaden the tested dimensionality and physical regimes beyond v1's four PDE cases. Existing PDE and CelebA coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 1-19 retain the same methods. The new PDE tests reuse the existing PINN baseline pool. Newly cited Jacobian-descent and dual-cone methods are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.13 adds an evaluation design varying cosine-decay schedules, constant learning rates, collocation sample counts and boundary/interior sampling ratios. Table 23 also specifies training allocations for the three new PDE cases. The stated protocols for retained experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic learning-rate and sampling sensitivity analyses in Tables 24-27 and Figure 26. Appendix A.11 also investigates unresolved anisotropic structure and explicitly examines chaotic dynamics as a failure case. Existing direction-weight and momentum analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three runs with different random seeds and report means and standard deviations. Added results follow this existing practice; no increased run count, new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1-19 are retained, while Tables 20-22 and 24-27 add substantial benchmark and sensitivity results. For example, PNd MSE is (0.415 +/- 0.052) x 10^-6 for M-ConFIG versus (1.916 +/- 0.284) x 10^-6 for Adam. Added findings also include incomplete HeatMS reconstruction and failure to capture chaotic KS dynamics.

T1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds a short storage-complexity argument giving O(nm) costs for per-loss gradients and momentum. The convergence theorems, assumptions and proofs, and the existence and equivalence arguments in A.1-A.4, are retained rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: v2 foregrounds provable convergence in the abstract and introduction as an explicit contribution, although the supporting proofs already existed in v1. The principal conflict-free optimization, momentum acceleration and PINN/MTL performance claims remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v1 mainly discusses M-ConFIG's degradation with many losses and its memory requirements. v2 adds substantive applicability boundaries: loss balancing alone cannot resolve anisotropic scaling or chaotic dynamics. It explains the KS failure through multiscale derivative-resolution difficulties and discusses architectural changes and causality as complementary directions.

D1.justification: Appendices A.11-A.12 document the new PDEs' equations, domains, boundary/initial conditions and training sample allocations and budgets. Existing architecture, optimizer settings, sampling procedure, hardware and code-access information are retained; training details move from A.11 to A.12.

R1.justification: v2 adds Quinton and Rey's Jacobian descent, Hwang and Lim's concurrent dual-cone gradient descent, and Hao et al.'s PINNacle benchmark. These modestly extend positioning and benchmark attribution; the existing related-work discussion is largely retained.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing exposition remain intact. Changes include local abstract and runtime-explanation edits, additional subsection headings, appendix organization, and conversion to author-year citations and conference headings.

P2.justification: v2 adds solution-comparison and sampling-sensitivity displays in Figures 23-26, seven benchmark/ablation result tables, and an expanded settings table. It also adopts ICLR headers and typography, changes table rules, and resizes or relocates retained figures and tables.

improvement.justification: The challenging PDE tests and hyperparameter ablations provide useful evidence about robustness and applicability beyond v1. Explicit HeatMS and KS failure discussions also clarify limitations. However, the new Section 4.1 claim of consistent superiority on challenging PDEs overstates Table 22, where neither variant leads and M-ConFIG performs worse than Adam. The added evidence improves the paper, but its summary claims are not fully aligned with that evidence.
